chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Ibn Abdillah al-Dari narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Salih ibn Sa'id al-Qammam, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Every Nāsibī ( enemy of the Ahl al-Bayt), even if he worships and strives (in worship), will become one of the people of this verse: 'A laboring Nāsibī will enter burning fire.'

key_terms.اجْتَهَدَ: Strived; exerted effort in religious practice
key_terms.تَعَبَّدَ: Worshipped; engaged in acts of devotion
key_terms.نَاراً حامِیَهً: Burning fire; a specific type of Hellfire
key_terms.نَاصِبٍ: Nāsibī; one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the fate of a Nāsibī who worships diligently?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) establishes that the core determinant of salvation is Wilayat (divine authority), asserting that a Nāsibī’s religious efforts are rendered void by their enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt. This hadith from *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the Shia theological principle that correct belief in leadership supersedes ritual practice, linking the 'burning fire' to the specific consequence of denying Imam Ali’s (a.s.) right. The citation underscores the severity of sectarian enmity as a distinct category of spiritual failure.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said, “The enemy of Ahle Bayt (a.s.)  is  an  example  of  that  verse  that:  Laboring,  toiling. Entering into burning fire (of Hell).”
